observations: Photo 0: a yellow steel LPG cooking gas cylinder with a protective collar ring and a foot ring, standing on a marble floor.
Photo 0: handwritten marker numbers on the shoulder and a shop sticker with phone numbers on the collar; the stamped tare and capacity marks on the collar are not readable.
Photo 0: paint is faded and dirty with small chips; valve is only partly visible behind the collar.
Photos 1 and 2: a different cylinder, blue, with a round globe logo on the body whose name is partly hidden by the watermark.
Photos 1 and 2: blue cylinder collar rim is worn black with chipped paint, body has scrapes and rust at the base edge.
Photo 2: the blue cylinder's brass valve is tarnished and grimy, not a new valve.
All photos: dealer watermark 'Petronjay Business' and 'Posted on Jiji'; no capacity, test date or tare stamp can be read on either cylinder.
Both cylinders look like mid-size household cylinders, consistent in proportion with a 12.5kg size, but the size is not marked legibly.

read_from: photos 1 and 2 cylinder shape and collar

claims.evidence: The shape and proportions fit a 12.5kg household cylinder, but no capacity or tare stamp is readable in any photo, and two different cylinders are shown.
No test date stamp or certificate shown in any photo.
No clip of a soapy water leak test at the valve and seams.
Photo 2 shows the blue cylinder's valve tarnished and grimy; the yellow cylinder's valve in photo 0 is not clearly shown.

risks.risk: Two different cylinders appear in the photos, so the one delivered is unknown
risks.proof: Photo of the exact cylinder being sold with a handwritten note bearing today's date
risks.if_unproven: as the worse of the two cylinders shown

risks.risk: Actual capacity may be smaller than 12.5kg
risks.proof: Close photo of the stamped capacity and tare weight on the collar
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest size consistent with the photos

risks.proof: Clip of soapy water applied to the valve and welds with the cylinder pressurised, showing no bubbles

risks.risk: Cylinder may be past its retest date or internally corroded
risks.proof: Close photo of the stamped manufacture and test dates on the collar
risks.if_unproven: as out of test, needing retest

risks.risk: Cylinder is sold empty, gas content unknown
risks.proof: Photo of the cylinder on a scale showing gross weight against the stamped tare

proof_requests: Photo of the exact cylinder for sale with a dated handwritten note
Close photo of the stamped capacity, tare weight and test date on the collar
Clip of a soapy water leak test at the valve
Photo of the cylinder on a scale
response.reason: A household cooking gas cylinder is a plain good identified by type, so it can be priced at its worst case as a used empty cylinder needing a valve and retest. The new valve claim is contradicted by photo 2, and the two different cylinders shown mean the worse one sets the price until the seller shows the exact unit.
